correctness.rationale: Gaussian Fourier integration gives the nonzero factor exp(−pi xi^2−2 pi i xi x) times 1+2q cosh(w)+2q^4 cosh(2w), where q=exp(−pi Delta^2) and w=2 pi Delta(xi+i x). Exponentiation gives a bijective cylinder coordinate with the reciprocal quartic of degree four and nonzero constant term. The quadratic in cosh(w) has discriminant 4q^2(2s−1)(4s^2+2s−1) with s=q^2. The values at y=±1 stay positive; the minimum of 1−2q+2q^4 for q>0 is 1−3/(2·4^(1/3))>0. Thus the inverse cosh never coalesces at its branch values. The two real roots lie in (−1,1) near s=1, meet at −1/sqrt(2) at s=1/2, become conjugate in the next interval, and meet below −1 at s_B; they remain below −1 for s<s_B. In the conjugate regime the upper-left root has one inverse with positive real part and angle in (pi/2,pi), and reciprocal and conjugate symmetry produce exactly the rectangle. Double roots pull back to double zeros because sinh(w) is nonzero there. Holomorphic multiplicity becomes negative phase winding in the reversed (x,xi) orientation; the nonzero prefactor adds no local winding. As q tends to zero the two root moduli are 1/(2q) and 1/(2q^3) up to relative O(q^2), yielding the stated midpoint errors after applying arcosh. The support script was inspected, not executed; its finite comparisons are not used for completeness.
residual_risks: Only the exact five-tone Gaussian model is covered; the proof makes no stability or zero-detection claim.

value.rationale: A global classification in a tractable interference model answers where every phase zero is, how zeros collide, and which geometries persist as the frequency gap changes. These are substantively useful statements beyond exhibiting a few zeros or plotting ridge maxima. The frozen package nonetheless does not add a distinct result beyond the exact catalogue coverage.
